name: Knockshegowna

appeared as a calf one evening

name may mean Fairy Calf Hill

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Knockshegowna is an Irish mythological site. It rises over the rolling land of north Tipperary, a region full of fairy mound tales. The hill is held to be the sidhe, or palace, of Una, an Irish fairy queen. One evening she came to him as a calf. A piper named Laurence Hoolahan would not stop his tipsy playing. Una spoke in human words and took him by surprise. He climbed onto her back. In a second the pair flew through the air and set down at the River Shannon, ten miles away. Una was struck that the piper showed no fear. Perhaps he was too drunk to care. Pleased by his courage, she let him go on piping on that hill for as long as he wanted. The yarn may grow from a misreading of the hill name as Fairy Calf Hill.
